bills.title: A resolution expressing support for the designation of the first week of August 2026, as "National Community Health Center Week", encouraging all people of the United States to participate by visiting their local community health center, and celebrating the important partnership between community health centers and the communities they serve.
bills.status: Submitted in the Senate, considered, and agreed to without amendment and with a preamble by Unanimous Consent. (consideration: CR S4553; text: CR S4568-4569)
bills.nexus: This resolution has no direct nexus to Treasury authorities, funding streams, or regulatory jurisdiction, as it is a purely ceremonial Senate resolution designating an awareness week for community health centers. Treasury Legislative Affairs does not need to track this bill for implementation or risk purposes.

bills.title: Critical Mineral and Extraction Tax Parity Act
bills.status: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.
bills.nexus: S. 5330 falls squarely within Treasury's jurisdiction because it would amend the Internal Revenue Code to adjust tax treatment for critical mineral extraction, directly engaging the Office of Tax Policy and IRS administration. Treasury must assess implementation complexity around defining qualifying minerals, preventing revenue leakage, and ensuring consistency with existing depletion and expensing provisions.

bills.title: Fairness in Foreign Filing Act
bills.status: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.
bills.nexus: S. 5173 touches Treasury's international tax authority and IRS administration because it addresses the treatment of foreign patent or IP filing fees, which can affect deductions, cost-sharing arrangements, or expense allocation rules under the Internal Revenue Code. Treasury and IRS would bear implementation responsibility for any regulatory guidance needed to define "fairness" standards and prevent taxpayers from manipulating cross-border IP structures to shift income.

bills.title: Homeowners Premium Tax Reduction Act of 2026
bills.status: Referred to the House Committee on Ways and Means.
bills.nexus: H.R. 9978 would amend the Internal Revenue Code to provide a tax deduction or credit for homeowners' insurance premiums, directly implicating IRS's administration of individual income tax provisions under Treasury's Office of Tax Policy. Treasury faces implementation risk around revenue scoring, rulemaking to define eligible premiums, and potential interaction with existing casualty loss and itemized deduction rules.

bills.title: Increasing Opportunity For Reindustrialization Act
bills.status: Referred to the House Committee on Ways and Means.
bills.nexus: H.R. 10006 falls within Treasury's purview because tax incentives or credits tied to domestic manufacturing reindustrialization would be administered through the Internal Revenue Service and designed in coordination with the Office of Tax Policy. Treasury faces implementation risk in structuring any new credits or deductions to prevent abuse, ensure revenue scoring accuracy, and align with existing IRC provisions.

bills.title: Retirement Simplification and Clarity Act
bills.status: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.
bills.nexus: S. 5156 falls squarely within Treasury's purview because it amends the Internal Revenue Code's qualified retirement plan provisions, directly implicating IRS and the Office of Tax Policy's regulatory and guidance authority. Treasury's implementation risk centers on the need to issue conforming regulations and updated plan qualification guidance, with potential revenue scoring consequences that require coordination with JCT.

bills.title: Strengthening Taxpayer Advocacy Act
bills.status: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.
bills.nexus: S. 5162 directly implicates the Office of the Taxpayer Advocate, a statutory office within IRS under Treasury's purview, by potentially altering its authority, independence, or case-handling procedures under IRC Section 7803(c). Treasury must assess implementation burden on IRS operations and any risk that expanded advocacy mandates could constrain audit, collection, or compliance functions.

bills.title: A bill to amend the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to modify procedural requirements for penalties and disallowance periods.
bills.status: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.
bills.nexus: S. 5143 directly amends the Internal Revenue Code, placing it squarely within IRS jurisdiction under Treasury's oversight of tax administration and compliance enforcement. Changes to penalty procedures and disallowance periods carry revenue-scoring implications and could constrain IRS operational flexibility in audit and collection workflows.

bills.title: A bill to amend the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to improve the notice and review procedure with respect to multi-year bans on claiming credits.
bills.status: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.
bills.nexus: S. 5141 amends the Internal Revenue Code to modify procedural rules governing multi-year bans on tax credits, directly implicating IRS administration under Treasury's Tax Policy and IRS oversight authorities. Treasury must assess implementation risk around revised notice requirements and any expanded taxpayer review rights that could affect audit workflows and refund integrity programs.

bills.title: A bill to amend the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to improve the process for providing refunds to taxpayers.
bills.status: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.
bills.nexus: S. 5142 directly implicates IRS authority under the Internal Revenue Code, placing implementation responsibility on the IRS Commissioner and the Treasury Office of Tax Policy to assess any changes to refund procedures, timelines, or appropriations requirements. The principal risk is operational: modifications to refund processing could affect IRS system architecture, improper payment exposure, and Treasury's cash management obligations under the Improper Payments Elimination and Recovery Act.

bills.title: A bill to amend the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to eliminate installment agreement fees for certain individuals.
bills.status: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.
bills.nexus: S. 5144 directly amends the Internal Revenue Code and would affect IRS user-fee authority under IRC Section 6159, which falls under Treasury's Office of Tax Policy and IRS administration. Eliminating installment agreement fees for certain taxpayers would reduce IRS cost-recovery revenue and require Treasury to assess fiscal impact and potentially revise fee regulations under 31 U.S.C. 9701.

bills.title: Harley Jacobsen Clinical Trial Participant Income Exemption Act of 2026
bills.status: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.
bills.nexus: S. 5127 would amend the Internal Revenue Code to exempt clinical trial participant payments from gross income, directly implicating IRS's tax expenditure authority and Treasury's Office of Tax Policy's responsibility for scoring and drafting any associated guidance. The implementation risk centers on defining qualifying payments without creating a broad exclusion that erodes the tax base or invites misclassification of other compensation as exempt research income.

bills.title: Strengthening EFIN Confirmation for User Reliability and Electronic (SECURE) Tax Filing Act
bills.status: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.
bills.nexus: S. 5111 directly implicates IRS authority under Treasury, specifically the Return Preparer Office's administration of Electronic Filing Identification Numbers (EFINs), which are the credentialing mechanism the agency uses to authorize paid preparers to submit returns electronically. The implementation risk centers on any new verification or confirmation requirements Treasury and IRS would need to operationalize within the e-file system, carrying potential burdens on IT infrastructure, preparer compliance timelines, and taxpayer filing continuity.

bills.title: Never Forget the Victims of Terrorism: Joseph D. Mistrulli and Alan Kleinberg USVSST Fund Solvency Act
bills.status: Referred to the House Committee on the Judiciary.
bills.nexus: The bill amends the United States Victims of State Sponsored Terrorism Fund, which is administered by a Special Master under DOJ but funded through fines and penalties collected and transferred by Treasury's offices, including FinCEN and the forfeiture programs. Treasury's risk angle centers on any new solvency or mandatory transfer requirements that could affect its collections pipeline, fund balance management, and interagency remittance obligations.

bills.title: Increasing Opportunity For Reindustrialization Act
bills.status: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.
bills.nexus: S. 4606 falls within Treasury's purview because the Committee on Finance referral signals tax or trade provisions that would likely require IRS or Office of Tax Policy to draft implementing guidance or regulations. Treasury's implementation risk centers on designing any new credits, deductions, or incentive structures tied to domestic manufacturing in a way that is administrable and revenue-scored accurately.

bills.title: TAS Act
bills.status: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.
bills.nexus: S. 3931, the TAS Act, directly implicates the Office of the Taxpayer Advocate by proposing changes to the statutory authority and independence of the Taxpayer Advocate Service under IRC Section 7803(c). Treasury must monitor this bill because any expansion of TAS's autonomy or case-acceptance criteria could constrain IRS operational flexibility and create administrative cost and workload pressures across the agency.
